alignments.note: Light verb plus complement 'took hold', headed on the complement (rule 44); the 'of' is the preposition the English verb needs to reach the suffixed object and joins the verb's unit (rule 44).

Comparative כְּ rendered by the two-word 'as of', headed on 'as' (rule 24). Competing reading: 'of' as the participle's supplied helper; the 'of' states the comparison rather than anything of the woman, so it was kept with the preposition.
Assimilated article; the ASV writes 'a', not 'the' (rule 12).

Substantival participle 'she who gives birth' rendered 'a woman in travail'; the supplied noun phrase joins the participle (rule 46) and the indefinite article is the noun phrase's (rule 15). Head on 'travail' as the word carrying the lexeme of יָלַד (rule 31).
